topic: Lobster0: Self-Hosted OpenClaw-Inspired AI Agent With Persistent Memory

key_points: A self-hosted, private-by-default personal agent; one Python Core reaches TUI, Feishu, Telegram and Discord via isolated channel pipelines
18 Core tools (system, files, search, HTTPS, exact-argv CLI, Memory surfaces) plus 8 optional isolated Browser tools; Browser disabled by default
OpenAI-compatible Provider (default deepseek-v4-pro); the model proposes Tool Calls that the Core validates, risk-scores, binds approvals, executes, audits, and recovers
Persistent Memory Autopilot: owner-scoped Markdown truth (memory/owners/<owner>/memory.md), async capture, FTS5/CJK retrieval, promote/review/conflict/correct/forget/TTL governance
Four permission modes - SAFE / SMART / AUTOPILOT / YOLO - with non-disableable hard boundaries (sensitive paths, SSRF, workspace)
Explanability by default: Turn, ToolRun, Approval, Delivery, Channel Inbox/Outbox persisted in SQLite; redacted logs; /memory rebuild, doctor drift checks
Privacy-by-default: secrets rejected at boundaries and never enter prompts/logs/Memory; groups and non-owners fail closed; cross-channel only for verified Owner DMs

Status: Phase 6.5 IMPLEMENTATION PASS - 1005/1005 Python unit tests, 41/41 TUI, 14/14 Browser Worker, 39/39 Agent offline cases, 660/660 channel soak; Feishu live verified, Telegram/Discord live gates pending

Current only release is v0.7.0 prerelease (RELEASE CANDIDATE / PUBLIC GATES PENDING); installable via wheel with uv (curl + uv tool install); install.sh one-line installer returns 404 until a stable ship
OpenClaw is the original project Lobster0 is inspired by; open-source AI assistant that runs on your own computer and meets you in channels (Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram...)
Reached massive traction - ~247K GitHub stars, 47.7K forks by March 2026, ~4 months after Nov 2025 launch as Warelay; rebranded twice (Clawdbot then Moltbot then OpenClaw)
Gateway architecture: a single persistent Node.js Gateway process binds to localhost:18789, maintains state in SQLite, orchestrates LLM + tools + protocol adapters
Persistent memory via injected prompt files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, TOOLS.md) and MEMORY.md; a background heartbeat cron can wake the agent and run tasks without a prompt
Large ClawHub skills registry (~13,729 community skills); security concerns documented (prompt injection, Clawdbot compromise); ships as a free self-hosted gateway with data staying on your hardware

Positions OpenClaw vs cloud assistants: execution (runs commands, does not just suggest), persistent memory (survives restarts via local MEMORY.md), proactive heartbeat (cron tasks fire without prompting)
Cost: free to self-host; your cost is a VPS + Node runtime + API key. No SaaS tier, no per-message pricing
Who it is for: developers/power users who want a persistent self-hosted agent that acts rather than advises; NOT for non-technical founders

A Grok research team published a ~10-page academic paper treating OpenClaw as a socio-technical phenomenon - the Lobster framing - analyzing its Lobster-Tank architecture and documented vulnerabilities
Frames OpenClaw as evidence that user-sovereign, locally-run agents can reach mainstream adoption without corporate infrastructure backing
Continuity across fragmented channels: start a task in Telegram, continue in Discord without losing semantic context; OAuth handled locally so credentials never transit third-party servers
ClaudeClaw: a developer pattern for building OpenClaw-style autonomous agents on Claude Code using a PostToolUse HTTP hook system (localhost:8080/events) to react to tool events
Shows the broader ecosystem trend: OpenClaw-style autonomy is being reimplemented on other agent harnesses (Claude Code, Copilot) rather than only the original gateway

stats.fact: Lobster0 was created 2026-08-07 and has ~103 GitHub stars, 14 forks, MIT license, written in Python, topics ai-agent/personal-agent/self-hosted/tool-calling (as of 2026-09-12)
Latest release is v0.7.0, marked prerelease (RELEASE CANDIDATE / PUBLIC GATES PENDING); no stable release or git tag beyond v0.7.0 exists yet

Project status: 1005/1005 Python unit tests PASS, 41/41 TUI TypeScript tests, 14/14 Browser Worker (real headless Chrome), 39/39 active offline Agent cases, 660/660 channel soak rounds, 15/15 automation (300/300), 18/18 browser (360/360)
Lobster0 exposes 18 Core tools plus 8 optional Browser tools (open, snapshot, click, type, press, scroll, screenshot, close); Browser disabled by default with a dedicated Chromium Profile
Supported platforms: Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Debian 12/13, RHEL/Rocky/Alma 9/10, macOS 13+ (x86_64 + arm64); native Windows, WSL, Alpine/musl, Android/Termux explicitly unsupported

Install: curl the wheel from GitHub Releases then uv tool install --python 3.12 (wheel with feishu extra); requires no preinstalled Node/pnpm; the one-line install.sh currently returns 404 (no stable release)

Memory Autopilot: owner-scoped Markdown truth + rebuildable SQLite projections; FTS5/CJK retrieval; async writes with atomic remember; promote/review/conflict/correct/forget/TTL/weekly-review governance

For context, parent OpenClaw reached ~247,000 GitHub stars and ~47,700 forks by March 2026 (~4 months after its Nov 2025 launch as Warelay), after rebranding twice; the ClawHub registry has ~13,729 skills

Lobster0 default permission mode is autopilot (configs without tools.mode default to autopilot); it trusts only the local entry point + verified Owner DMs; groups and other users auto-downgraded; hard boundaries are never disableable

angles: Private-by-default vs the hype: Lobster0 deliberately eschews OpenClaw's 20+ channel sprawl for a small-but-complete 4-channel core with auditable, explainable local state
Four permission modes (SAFE/SMART/AUTOPILOT/YOLO) as a governance story - autonomy with non-disableable hard boundaries, differentiated from OpenClaw's single-user full-access default
The honest release-status framing: v0.7.0 is an unmarked prerelease, IMPLEMENTATION PASS not live PASS - a transparency angle that undercuts typical agent hype
Memory Autopilot as the real differentiator: cross-channel owner-scoped memory with write governance, unlike OpenClaw's simple MEMORY.md prepend
Self-hosted agent comparison ladder: OpenClaw (mature, huge ecosystem) vs Lobster0 (young, private-first, evidence-driven) vs cloud agents (ChatGPT/Claude) - where each fits
One Core, many entry points: TUI + Feishu/Telegram/Discord sharing one AgentRuntime with isolated transport/delivery pipelines and failure domains
